seoTitle: How to Verify and Link Your Bank Account for eBay Payouts
metaDescription: Learn how to verify and link a bank account on eBay for seller payouts, including the micro-deposit process and fixes for common linking errors.
intro: Getting paid for eBay sales comes down to one setup step in your account: linking and verifying the bank account that receives payouts. This guide walks through that process end to end — adding your account details, clearing eBay's micro-deposit verification, and troubleshooting the errors that most often stall a new seller before their first payout lands. It applies whether you're setting this up for the first time as a new seller or switching to a different bank after using eBay for a while.

steps.heading: Open your eBay account and head to Payments
steps.body: Bank linking lives inside your account settings, reached through My eBay or Seller Hub depending on which view your account defaults to. Look for a Payments section under Account settings — this is the same place eBay shows your payout history and schedule once money starts moving, so it's worth bookmarking even after setup is done.

steps.heading: Add your bank account details
steps.body: Enter your bank's routing number and account number for the checking account you want payouts sent to. Double-check both numbers against a check or your bank's app before submitting — a single transposed digit is the single most common reason this step has to be redone, and it's easy to miss on a quick copy-paste.

steps.heading: Complete micro-deposit verification
steps.body: After you submit your account, eBay sends one or two small test deposits to confirm you actually own the account rather than just knowing its numbers. These typically show up within a couple of business days as small, oddly specific amounts on your bank statement or in your online banking activity. Once you see them, go back into eBay's verification screen and enter the exact amounts to complete the match.

steps.heading: Fix the most common linking errors
steps.body: If eBay rejects the account outright, the usual culprits are a mismatched account holder name, an account type eBay doesn't support for payouts (savings accounts sometimes cause issues where checking accounts don't), or a routing number that doesn't match the account number's bank. Re-check each field individually rather than re-submitting the whole form blind, since resubmitting an error unchanged just produces the same rejection.

steps.heading: Know what to expect once verification clears
steps.body: Once the account is verified, it becomes the default destination for payouts, and eBay will show it in your Payments settings alongside your payout schedule. This is also when you'll start seeing scheduled or on-demand payout options depending on your seller status, so it's worth reviewing the payout frequency settings at the same time rather than as a separate task later.

steps.heading: Update your bank details if you switch banks
steps.body: Nothing about this process is one-and-done — if you close an account or move banks, return to the same Payments settings to add the new account. eBay will require you to go through micro-deposit verification again for the new account even if the old one was already verified, since verification is tied to the specific account, not your seller profile as a whole.

faq.question: How long does eBay bank verification take?
faq.answer: Micro-deposit verification typically takes a couple of business days for the test deposits to appear in your bank account.

faq.question: Why does eBay keep rejecting my bank account?
faq.answer: This is usually due to a mismatched account name, an unsupported account type, or an incorrect routing number entered during setup.

faq.question: Can I use eBay with any bank?
faq.answer: eBay supports most major U.S. banks, including Bank of America, Chase, and Wells Fargo, as long as the account is a standard checking account.

faq.question: Can I change my bank account on eBay after it's verified?
faq.answer: Yes, you can update your linked bank account at any time from the same payment settings, though you'll need to verify the new account again from scratch.

faq.question: What if the micro-deposits never show up in my bank account?
faq.answer: Double-check the account and routing numbers you entered for typos, since a wrong number sends the deposits nowhere; if the details are correct, contact eBay support to have them reissued.
